loc.1.0:
With great skill, you guided your ship through the fighting military- and pirate ships and brought it into the closest open hangar at the pirate station. Before landing you managed to see the military base that so brazenly docked at the pirate habitation. You found its menacing appearance foreboding. But what are you going to do? Somebody's got to save everyone once again.

Extracting yourself from the ship, you were instantly immersed in the surrounding chaos. Everybody around was running, screaming, and waving their weapons. It looked like the pirates were preparing to give battle to the army boys. But not everything was what it seemed. You should have turned your back, because some rogue peleng tried to hijack your ship. You dragged him by his neck from the cabin and, as punishment, ordered him to explain how to get to the place where the soldiers are gathering to attack.
- "though the gates on the left," squeaked the pirate and spryly jerked out of your grasp.
Rather than chase him down, you started off to where he had directed. Getting where you needed to go proved to be easy. It was enough to move in the opposite direction of the pirates who were bolting away from the danger.
loc.5.0: A long way off you saw where the forces attacking the pirate base were gathering. Then your glance shifted to the control panel, surveying the enormous number of buttons you can push and switches you can switch. The fact that the purpose of most of these control mechanisms was entirely unknown to you didn't particularly hold you back. After all, the fate of the whole pirate enterprise was at stake. And considering that you had at your command three whole types of turrets, you involuntarily felt like a great strategist.
loc.5.1:
During the brief lulls between waves of fire, you got out from behind the control panel and went to see the battlefield. You never know - you might find something interesting. After a bit of searching among cyborg debris and soldier corpses, you discovered an <clr>entire box of mines<clrEnd> labelled "Super mines. GOST 13197-67", which had probably been defended by the soldiers attacking you. Mines can be highly relevant if an enemy breaks through your defensive lines...
Here your reflections as a military leader were interrupted by a new wave of enemy fire. Straining under its weight, you threw the box on your shoulder and hightailed it back behind the panel.
loc.5.2:
Filled with rage, you fearlessly look at the enemy forces advancing toward you. The defensive turrets behave like exemplary children under your careful and effective control.
The main panel displays the number of enemy forces destroyed:
- soldiers: [p21]
- cyborgs: [p22]
- heavy weapons: [p23]
loc.5.3:
One of the laser turrets couldn't withstand the heat from the continuous firing and splintered into small fragments in a deafening explosion.
The attacking forces noted this event with cries of joy.
Number of enemy forces destroyed:
- soldiers: [p21]
- cyborgs: [p22]
- heavy weapons: [p23]
loc.5.4:
You fired the rocket launchers, but the target was so close that the debris from the explosion both destroyed the enemy and damaged your control panel. You were barely able to drop down to avoid hurting yourself.
Number of enemy forces destroyed:
- soldiers: [p21]
- cyborgs: [p22]
- heavy weapons: [p23]
loc.5.5:
You finished your works and returned to the panel just in time - the enemy was already in range of your weapons.
Now the number of mines you have set is [p9], at a distance of <clr>50<clrEnd> meters from the control panel. An unpleasant surprise awaits enemies who make it to that point.
loc.5.6: You couldn't hold in an exclamation of joy when the lethal surprise you left detonated flawlessly, blasting your foes to smithereens. It's not in vain that maloq mothers teach their offspring that mines aren't toys. Not in vain, no sir.
loc.5.7: Most unfortunately, the box you searched turned out to be completely empty. After cursing whoever succeeded in removing everything useful from the box, you returned to behind the panel in a very nasty mood.
loc.5.8: Your joy knew no bounds when you found several rounds of the same caliber as your defense turrets. You seized your find and whirled back behind the panel, somewhat unsteady from the weight of the ammunition. Fortunately, you managed to do so just in time to begin deflecting the enemy attack.
loc.5.9: Apparently, your talent for strategy malfunctioned, because the enemy drew close enough to attack, while remaining alive and very dangerous. A torrent of gunfire hammered the control panel, riddling it with holes and triggering showers of sparks. You were forced to take refuge behind the panel, pressing buttons nearly blindly to avoid becoming a victim of the fragments flying every which way.
loc.11.0: Well, the first wave of attack was repelled. You proudly slapped the control panel with your hand, accidentally striking a couple of buttons. But nothing happened and you sighed deeply in relief. If the rest of the attacks are like that, it'll be a piece of cake.
loc.11.1: You beat back the second wave and even became somewhat worried, as if you were getting bored. Everything turned out to be painfully easy.
loc.11.2: The third wave concerned you - but just a little bit. As before, you have a feeling of invincibility.
loc.11.3: You handled the fourth wave and nervously examined the control panel, but everything seemed to be okay with it for now. But only the silly plush souvenir hanging on the frame of the panel was blown the shreds by a bullet. You considered this a bad sign.
loc.11.4: The fifth wave caused you great concern. If things continued in this vein, you would soon be without ammunition, facing several thousands of attacking enemy forces, and abusive words wouldn't likely be as effective against them as machine-gun fire.
loc.11.5: You exhaled and wiped your brow of the sweat which was pouring into your eyes. If you're honest with yourself, you panicked for a moment, especially when you saw a rocket flying straight at you. Fortunately, it was knocked off course. Only this left you alive and the control panel, though thoroughly battered, still functional.
loc.11.6: After repulsing the next wave you became more like squeezed fruit than a proud space ranger. Your fingers ached as if, rather than currently pressing a button on the control panel, you were performing a piano solo at a concert for the peleng composer Mot Zart. The air around you grew warm from the operation of the turrets, enough so that you could have lit up a cigar. And the control panel's processor shorted out because it couldn't keep up with your commands.
loc.11.7: You exhaled and wiped your brow of the sweat which was pouring into your eyes. If you're honest with yourself, you panicked for a moment, especially when you saw a rocket flying straight at you. Fortunately, it was knocked off course. Only this left you alive and the control panel, though thoroughly battered, still functional.
loc.11.8: After repulsing this wave, you became more like squeezed fruit than a proud space ranger. Your fingers ached as if, rather than currently pressing a button on the control panel, you were performing a piano solo at a concert for the peleng composer Mot Zart. The air around you grew warm from the operation of the turrets, enough so that you could have lit up a cigar. And the control panel's processor shorted out because it couldn't keep up with your commands.
loc.12.0:
Unlikely, but true - it seemed - this was the last wave of attack and no one else would lay siege to your hangar. You suppressed the trembling in your knees and proudly drew yourself erect, putting one hand behind your back - and the other behind the lapel of your ranger outfit However, they'll write about your victory in the history books, if, of course, somebody takes your word for it, because there was not a single witness of your triumph left alive.
Perhaps it's time for you to pay the army boys a friendly visit of your own.
loc.13.0: You were in a large, dark, and perfectly empty hangar in front of the pirate base's utility tunnels. They had most likely already been captured by the enemy. Judging by the absolute silence in the hangar, none of the base's defenders wanted to be on the first line of defense of their own pirate nest.
loc.13.1:
You turned your head, studying the situation.
The airlock overlapping the hangar exit was completely closed off. Undoubtedly, somebody thought to block the soldiers' path before running away in disgrace. Near the hangar exit itself a small cubicle was attached to the wall. Through the glass you could see the blinking multi-colored lights of a control panel. And formidable turrets for laser guns, machine guns, and rockets for even the most exacting taste, were mounted along the perimeter of the hangar.
loc.13.2:
The closed hatch towers above you in all its impregnability.
You examined it but could not find any buttons or levers to open it.
loc.13.3: The control panel was entirely dotted with different little buttons, tiny levers, lights, and displays. Judging by their number, one gets the impression that you could use it to control the whole pirate base. However, that's unlikely.
loc.15.0:
You stared intently at the control panel and didn't take long to guess how it works. Directly in the center of the panel was a large, round, and utterly arousing red button, to which a scrap of paper with a clumsy note was attached: "Do not press! Airlock!!!".
Unfortunately, if you want to break into the military base and repel the onslaught of soldiers - you're going to have to press it. And this must be done as quickly as possible, before the soldiers have moved all of their troops and heavy machinery up to the airlock.
loc.16.0:
A piercing alarm screamed, red reflections of the emergency lights swept across the walls, the hydraulics began to hiss, and the airlock slowly moved upward, clearing the path into the military base.
Fortunately, a couple thousand maloqs armed to the teeth weren't waiting on the other side of the airlock. Rather there were just a few soldiers who had been assigned to guard the airlock until a way could be found to open it and penetrate the pirate base. Unfortunately, just one of these soldiers was enough to notice the airlock opening and activate the alarm. Their alarm now joined with yours to create a true cacophony that tortured your ears.
As soon as the airlock had opened completely, the control panel's main screen woke up, and instead of displaying greetings it indicated that a break-in had been detected on the first level. You fully agreed with it and pressed the button labeled "Activate defense turrets".
"Note that you may currently synchronize {[p2]+[p3]+1} turrets," informed the panel.

Thus, you had laser-, machine-gun-, and rocket turrets at your disposal. You can give preference to the laser turrets of the machine-gun turrets, or you can take them approximately equally. Laser turrets have a shorter range and quickly overheat when fired, but they have the advantage of not being limited by ammunition. Machine-gun turrets, on the other hand, shoot farther, but their supply of cartridges is limited. You, of course, would prefer rocket launchers, but your inexperienced hands managed to activate <clr>only one<clrEnd> of them.
loc.16.1:
1. <clr>Rocket turrets<clrEnd>
Sighting distance - 200 m
Maximum range - 500 m
Type of charges: exploding.
Warning! To avoid being hit by fragments, do not use to destroy targets that are too close.

2. <clr>Machine-gun turrets<clrEnd>
Sighting distance - 80 m
Maximum range - 260 m
Type of charges - average caliber rounds.
Machine-gun turrets are equipped with an automatic ammo-feeding system and do not need to be reloaded manually.

3. <clr>Laser turrets<clrEnd>
Sighting distance - 51 m
Maximum range - 170 m
Type of charges - high-temperature energy impulses.
As a huge amount of heat is generated during use, you must carefully watch the temperature and not allow temperature of the action to reach 100 degrees.

Remember that when shooting at a distance greater than the sighting distance, inflicting the maximum possible damage on the target is not guaranteed.

If the closest line of defense is breached, <clr>broad spectrum mines<clrEnd> should be used. Mines are highly effective at destroying the enemy's machinery. Due to the presence of electromagnetic components, mines should be installed no closer than 50 meters from the defensive control panel.

param.0.crit:
You hid behind the control panel until it was reminiscent of sieve. All the lights went out, bullets knocked out the buttons, and the levels fell off, having nothing to be attached to. The defensive turrets died impotently when the commands stopped coming.
The last thing you saw through the holes in the panel body was an army of soldiers advancing on you. And then the panel finally collapsed, depriving you of your last defense.
